entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of the India seeking the following reliefs:-
"to issue a writ, order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declare the action of respondent No.4 and their staff trying to dispossess the petitioner from the agricultural land measuring an extent of Ac.1.78 Cents in Sy.No.50/2A, 53/4A of Gundisettipalle Village, Shanthipuram Mandal, Chittoor C P Hari Reddy vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25236051/
1 District without issuing notification under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 for acquiring the land of the petitioner at the behest of the unofficial respondents as illegal, arbitrary and in violation of Article14, 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondent No.4 not to interfere and dispossess the petitioner from the agricultural land measuring an extent Ac.1.78 Cents in Sy.No.50/2A, 53/4A of Gundisettipalle Village, Shanthipuram Mandal, Chittoor District and pass such other order."

entities.text: Chittoor C P Hari Reddy vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
2. During hearing, learned counsel for the petitioner, without touching the merits of the case,
requested this Court to issue a direction to the respondents not to interfere and dispossess the petitioner from the subject property without following due process of law.
3. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue submits that, if the petitioner is in possession of the subject property, the respondents would follow due process of law.

4. Having regard to the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Assistant Government Pleader for the respondents, it is observed that when the petitioner is in settled possession and enjoyment of the subject property, he cannot be dispossessed, without following due process of law in view of the law declared by the Apex Court in "Rame Gowda (dead)
by L.Rs. v. M.Varadappa Naidu (Dead) by L.Rs.1".

entities.text:
Rame Gowda (dead)
by L.Rs. v. M.Varadappa Naidu (Dead)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, if the petitioner is in possession of the subject property, the respondents are directed not to interfere and dispossess the petitioner from the subject property, except by following due process of law.
5. With the above direction, the writ petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel miscellaneous application, pending, if any, shall also stand closed.

VENKATESWARLU NIMMAGADDA, J 09.05.2025 TPS 2004 (1) SCC 769 HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE VENKATESWARLU NIMMAGADDA WRIT PETITION NO:13141 of 2025 09.05.2025 TPS C P Hari Reddy vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25236051/
